prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of an indoor bouldering wall (~1.5–3 m in front of the camera wearer) meeting padded floor mats below, as the camera tilts downward across the 5 frames. It separates four depth layers: the camera wearer's own raised right hand in the lower-right foreground (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach) in frames 3–4, a black-shirted bystander entering the near left foreground (~0.5–0.8 m, also within arm's reach) in frames 4–5 who partially occludes a grey-shirted bystander standing ~0.8–1.0 m further back (~1.5–2.2 m from the camera) on the left, and a climber ~1.5–2 m to their right who drops from high on the upper wall (~1.5–2.2 m away, partly cropped at the top in frames 1–4) onto the floor mat (~2.5–3 m away) in frame 5. All three other people face away from the camera wearer—the two left bystanders in right-facing profile toward the wall and the climber facing the wall then downward toward the mat—while the climber's holds (frames 1–3) and the mat (frame 5) lie within the climber's reach. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the relief of protruding climbing holds and the exact foreground separation between the two overlapping left-side bystanders immediately apparent. However, the map is unreliable in its per-frame auto-scaling—the wall and floor mat shift from mid-grey in frames 1–3 to nearly black in frames 4–5 when bright foreground figures enter—and it blurs the angled right-hand wall junction in frames 1–3.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete people and wall fixtures against the unlabelled climbing wall and floor mats across the 5 frames as the camera pans down to follow the descending climber. On the left, it segments the grey-shirted bystander (~1.5–2.2 m away, partly cut off by the left edge in frames 1–3) and the nearer black-shirted bystander (~0.5–0.8 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) who enters in front of and partially occludes her in frames 4–5, with both facing right toward the climber rather than looking at the camera wearer. To their right (~1.5–2 m away) and above, it tracks the climber descending from the upper wall (upper body cropped out of view in frames 1–4, ~1.5–2.5 m away) to a crouched posture on the floor mat (~2.5–3 m away, hands on the mat) in frame 5, as well as the camera wearer's own raised right arm and hand (~0.3–0.5 m away) in the lower-right of frames 3–4. While the masks clearly delineate the boundary between the two overlapping bystanders on the left in frames 4–5 where dark clothing blends in RGB, the map is highly unreliable in its class labels and background boundaries. Specifically, it misclassifies climbing holds as kitchenware or food ('fork', 'knife', 'spoon', 'apple', 'mouse', 'sports ball'), labels the angled yellow wall panel on the right as a 'knife' or merges it with the climber's 'person' mask in frame 3, and hallucinates a 'cell phone' on the grey-shirted bystander's chest in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body and hand skeletons in empty black space, capturing the torso and limb orientations of the grey-shirted bystander on the left (~1.5–2.2 m away) in frames 1, 4, and 5 and the camera wearer's raised right hand (~0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach) on the right in frames 3–4. The yellow torso, head, and leg keypoints show the grey-shirted bystander standing on the left facing right in profile toward the climbing wall (not looking toward the camera wearer) and shifting downward and slightly backward in the frame as the camera tilts down from frame 1 to frame 5. The magenta hand skeleton in frames 3–4 explicitly maps the five spread fingers and palm orientation of the camera wearer's right hand reaching upward into the right foreground (~1.5 m to the right of the bystanders and ~1.5–2 m in front of the wall), which is more geometrically explicit than in the RGB image alone. However, the pose map is severely incomplete and unreliable for full-scene spatial understanding because it misses the grey-shirted bystander completely in frames 2–3 where she is heavily cropped at the left margin. Furthermore, it fails to detect the nearer black-shirted bystander (~0.5–0.8 m away, partially occluding the grey-shirted bystander in frames 4–5) and completely omits the climber (~1.5–3 m away) both while partly cropped high on the wall in frames 1–4 and while crouched on the mat in frame 5.
